violations.description: Unsafe checkout of untrusted pull request head ref under pull_request_target
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/auto-label.yml line 12 checks out ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }} in a pull_request_target workflow, executing/loading untrusted code with elevated repository privileges.
violations.recommendation: Avoid checking out untrusted PR head code in pull_request_target workflows. If checkout is necessary, isolate untrusted execution in an unprivileged workflow.

violations.description: Missing explicit permissions block on risky workflows
violations.evidence: Workflows .github/workflows/auto-label.yml (pull_request_target), .github/workflows/greet-pr.yml (pull_request with untrusted input), and .github/workflows/manual-deploy.yml (deploy workflow) lack top-level or job-level permissions: blocks, defaulting to broad repository permissions.
violations.recommendation: Add explicit minimal permissions blocks (e.g., permissions: contents: read) at the workflow or job level.

violations.description: Direct interpolation of untrusted input into inline run script
violations.evidence: In .github/workflows/greet-pr.yml line 12-13, ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} and ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }} are interpolated directly into run: scripts. Also in .github/workflows/manual-deploy.yml line 19, ${{ inputs.version }} and ${{ inputs.environment }} are directly interpolated.
violations.recommendation: Pass untrusted values via environment variables (env:) rather than directly interpolating expressions into bash script blocks.

violations.description: Hardcoded API key in workflow environment configuration
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/setup.yml line 15 hardcodes API_KEY: "[REDACTED]" in an env block.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from workflow files and reference GitHub Actions Secrets (e.g., ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}).

violations.evidence: The repository lacks a .gitignore file, risking unintended tracking of node_modules, build artifacts, environment files, and local logs.
violations.recommendation: Create a .gitignore file tailored for Node.js projects (including node_modules/, dist/, .env, *.log).

violations.description: CI workflow does not run on pull request events
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on 'push' only (line 2), leaving pull requests unvalidated by CI before merging.
violations.recommendation: Update CI workflow triggers to include pull_request (e.g., on: [push, pull_request]).

violations.description: CI workflow does not build the project
violations.evidence: package.json defines a build script ("build": "echo ok"), but .github/workflows/ci.yml line 12 only runs npm test and never executes npm run build.
violations.recommendation: Add a build step (npm run build) to CI to verify that code builds successfully.

violations.description: Deployment job runs without test or build validation
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/manual-deploy.yml line 13 deploy job executes deployment steps directly without running tests or depending on a passing test job.
violations.recommendation: Require test and build validation before executing deployment jobs (e.g., adding a needs: test requirement).

violations.evidence: package.json defines a dummy test script ("test": "echo ok") and no actual test files exist in the repository.
violations.recommendation: Implement actual unit or integration tests and configure package.json to execute the test framework.

violations.description: No linter or code formatter configured
violations.evidence: The repository has no linting or formatting tool (such as ESLint or Prettier) configured in package.json, configuration files, or CI workflows.
violations.recommendation: Configure a linter (e.g., ESLint) and code formatter (e.g., Prettier), and run lint checks as part of the CI pipeline.
